Sofia — appreciate the note and the forecast. High-level proposal attached (RI-Proposal_v1.pdf) but calling out the key structuring options here so procurement has something to react to quickly: 

1) Commitment format: 36-month total committed $ with annual sub-targets (you can choose fixed-year caps or a flexible rolling wallet).

2) Laddered credit assignment (example):
   - Front-loaded: Year1 60% of wallet, Year2 25%, Year3 15% — gives best effective unit price in Year1 (we can surface a 12% term discount on Year1 unit rates under this shape).
   - Even: 33/33/33 — smaller first-year discount (typically ~8% term discount).
   - Back-loaded: 20/30/50 — we can support, but discount shifts to later years.

3) Rolling windows vs strict months:
   - Rolling monthly window: credits consumed on a 30/60/90-day rolling basis (preferred for bursty workloads).
   - Strict monthly drawdown: simpler billing alignment; true-ups at month-end.

4) True-ups & overage:
   - Monthly true-up with quarterly reconciliation. Overage billed at a pre-agreed premium (e.g., committed unit price + 30%) or drawn from a reserve tranche to smooth spikes.

5) Refunds / reallocation:
   - Standard: No cash refunds for unused prepay. We offer limited reallocation across years within the contract if usage variance <20% and with 30-day notice.

I'll set up a 30-minute sync to walk through the sample numbers (we can show how effective blended price moves with different shapes). Marissa and Karthik are on copy to confirm finance and engineering constraints.

Next step: please confirm which ladder shape Procurement prefers and whether a rolling window is required. I'll send a sample clause for the drawdown schedule and the DocuSign-ready term sheet once we align.

Priyom — quick finance perspective:

- Reallocation: we can allow inter-year reallocation up to 25% once per year without penalty; above that, a reallocation fee equal to 5% of the reallocated amount will apply. No cash refunds.

- Reserve tranche: we can structure a 10% reserve (kept in the wallet) that can be used for spikes and consumed before overage billing kicks in. This reduces surprise overage invoices and is common for bursty customers.

- Overage cap & pricing: recommend initial overage premium of committed rate + 25% with an annual cap (not to exceed 1.5x committed rate) — gives predictability.

- True-ups: monthly consumption reporting with quarterly reconciliations and an annual audit right.

I've attached a sample repayment/reallocation schedule (commit-schedule-xlsx.xlsx) and a short paragraph we can seed into the term sheet for Legal. If ProspectCo needs front-loaded credits >60% in Y1 (e.g., 70%), finance will ask for a higher early-term discount (we can push to 13% but need exec approval).

Cc: Legal will want any language that lets us preserve MRC if product usage materially falls below forecast.

— Marissa
